comparator.name: Natural Sciences
comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 formally adopted Faculty of Science EER; current 180-EC standard route
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 EER, Arts. 7.3–7.5, defines 60 EC first-year compulsory physics, mathematics, chemistry and biochemistry; 30 EC later shared compulsory courses; a 72-EC formal specialisation; 6 EC free electives; and a 12-EC Bachelor’s Internship and Report as individual final project. For the first-listed Physical Chemistry specialisation, 33 EC of named courses are required and 39 EC is restricted choice from eligible non-overlapping Faculty of Science bachelor courses and/or a permitted minor. Total: 60+30+33+39+6+12=180. The other two specialisations, Biophysics and Biochemistry, are mutually exclusive and are not mixed into this route. First-listed instances are used only for alternative course groups within the selected route; they are not UCR-matching selections. The 0-EC first-year Academic Skills subcomponent and RADAr assessment carry no additional credits. Prospective 2027–28 programme pages illustrate routes but the adopted 2026–27 EER controls requirements. The programme language is Dutch though most courses are taught in English.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target names no specialisation. The adopted EER offers three equally formal combinations of two natural sciences, each with a common 60-EC first year and 30-EC later core; it identifies no general unspecialised route. The first-listed Physical Chemistry option is the neutral official-order tie break after testing for a broader route, without reference to the UCR catalogue.

alternatives.label: Life, environmental & quantitative sciences
alternatives.labelReason: Life science, Earth and environmental science, mathematics, statistics, programming and data analysis form the programme’s balanced spine; the label does not imply dedicated physics or chemistry study.
alternatives.concept: Combine cellular and organismal biology with evolution, Earth systems, climate and environmental processes, using mathematics, programming, statistics, modelling and data analysis to investigate scientific problems. This is UCR’s strongest integrated natural-science response, while Radboud’s compulsory physics, chemistry and experimental physical-science sequence remain explicit gaps.
progression: Life-science, Earth-science, sustainability, programming and mathematical foundations precede cell biology, physiology, biochemistry, evolution, laboratory work, advanced mathematics, genetics, biogeochemistry and the applied research project. All formal prerequisites and exact planned offerings pass; six 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Molecular, cellular & biomedical biology
alternatives.labelReason: Molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, disease, laboratory work and computational analysis dominate; the label does not claim UCR supplies the route’s chemistry or physics.
alternatives.concept: Develop the target’s Biological-Chemical direction through molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, immunity, disease, laboratory work and quantitative analysis. UCR provides biological and biochemical study but not the analytical, organic, inorganic and physical chemistry or physics sequence of the Radboud route.
progression: Life-science, brain-and-behaviour, programming, mathematics, statistics and data foundations precede molecular biology, physiology, laboratory work, genetics, disease, immunity, pharmacology and advanced analysis. All formal prerequisites and exact planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: The first programme integrates life science with evolution, Earth systems, climate, sustainability and a broad mathematics line. The second concentrates on molecular, cellular and biomedical biology, replacing twelve environmental, Earth-system, evolution, sustainability and higher-mathematics courses with neuroscience, anatomy, immunity, pharmacology, disease, imaging and machine-learning courses. Each programme therefore contains 90 EC not found in the other, above the 30-EC floor.

candidates.label: Biophysics and biological-physical science
candidates.assessment: UCR can combine biology with mathematics and data analysis, but it has no mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics, quantum mechanics or experimental-physics sequence. A complete biophysics programme would therefore substitute methods and biomedical courses for the missing physics.

candidates.label: Physics, chemistry, nanoscience and materials
candidates.assessment: UCR has no chemistry or physics course sequence, nanoscience, materials or solid-state physics. Mathematics, Earth science and Biochemistry are specific neighbouring contributions but cannot sustain this physical-chemical direction; the absence of teacher qualification is secondary to the academic gap.

selection.assessment: The broad life, environmental and quantitative programme is UCR’s strongest integrated response. The Biological-Chemical direction supports a distinct molecular and biomedical second programme. The next direction, biophysics, fails because UCR lacks the necessary physics sequence; the still more physical-chemical and materials direction fails for the same reason plus the absence of chemistry, so production stops at two.

notes.text: Radboud Natural Sciences integrates physics, chemistry, biology and mathematics and, in the selected Physical Chemistry route, continues through quantum mechanics, spectroscopy, chemical bonding, advanced mechanics and electromagnetism. UCR can combine life, environmental and quantitative sciences and can develop a molecular-biological direction, but these are related-fields responses rather than reproductions of the full integrated physical-science curriculum.
